items.title: Viral video raises questions over safety of green-painted motorcycle lane
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A viral video showing several motorcyclists apparently losing control on a rain-soaked green-painted section of the Federal Highway motorcycle lane near Subang has raised questions over its safety in wet weather. The location is believed to be the Federal Highway motorcycle lane near Subang, Selangor. The Federal Highway motorcycle lane near Subang had previously drawn attention over the use of green-painted sections at several points along the route.

items.title: Haze worsens in Serian, schools closed
items.summary: KUCHING: The air pollution index (API) in Serian worsened, exceeding the very unhealthy level this morning. The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System recorded an API reading of 221 in Serian as of 6am, placing it in the very unhealthy category. Other districts that recorded unhealthy API readings were Kuching (194), Samarahan (188), Bintulu (170), Sri Aman (168), Samalaju (164), Sarikei (160), Sibu (159), Mukah (155) and Miri (148).

items.title: Oil up almost two pct as Iran's president vows to never surrender
items.summary: HOUSTON: Oil prices were up almost two per cent a barrel on Wednesday in choppy trade, as traders evaluated Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's vow never to surrender, a day after US President Donald Trump warned he could "annihilate" Iran. Brent crude futures rose US$1.84, or 1.85per cent, to US$101.09 a barrel by 11:11 a.m. EDT while West Texas Intermediate futures gained 69 cents, or 0.76per cent, to US$91.two1. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said later that a diesel export ban would not work.

items.title: Sarawak haze map darkens with Lundu’s sharp rise, Serian and Kanowit still choking
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 24 — Air quality in Lundu deteriorated to the ‘Very Unhealthy’ level this morning, joining Serian and Kanowit as the three locations in Sarawak recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 200. Both locations remained in the ‘Very Unhealthy’ category. Kuching continued to record ‘Unhealthy’ air quality, with its API increasing from 185 to 195.

items.title: Woman killed, five family members injured in Tanah Merah crash
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A woman was killed while her husband and four children were injured in an accident involving their Perodua Alza and a Toyota Hilux at Jalan Rantau Panjang-Panglima Bayu, Tanah Merah, yesterday. Tanah Merah district police chief Supt Mohd Haki Hasbullah said Tengku Ziarulwida Tuan Zainudin, 39, who was a passenger in the Perodua Alza, was killed on the spot in the 3pm incident. He said preliminary investigations showed that the Perodua Alza, driven by Tengku Ziarulwida's husband, Mohd Saifulzawawi Ghani, 39, collided head-on with the Toyota Hilux.

items.title: #NSTviral: Teacher's 16 weeks lesson plan reduced to soggy scraps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sixteen weeks of carefully prepared lesson plans were reduced to soggy scraps after a teacher's bag fell from her scooter, scattering her documents across a wet road and into the path of passing vehicles. The practicum teacher, who goes by @arahhsn on Threads, said she had placed her bag on the scooter's footrest before it fell, scattering her stamped lesson plans and other paperwork. Sixteen weeks of lesson plans, which had already been stamped, were scattered and destroyed on the road.

items.title: Australia says OpenAI agent hacked into government website
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia said on Wednesday an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorised access to files, in what could be the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website. The breach is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the United States, coming on top of several recent breaches globally by rogue AI agents that have alarmed governments and companies. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the medical statistics portal of a government agency responsible for non-sensitive health data and statistics, including public medical spending.

items.title: Ipoh police arrest three foreign students after man dies from brutal head trauma
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 24 — Police confirmed the arrest of three foreign male students from a private higher learning institution believed to be involved in the murder of a local man in Kampung Kuchai here on Sept 18. Ipoh police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the suspects, aged between 17 and 20, were detained at their apartment unit yesterday. Muhammad Najib said following investigations, police detained the three suspects to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

items.title: RoS suspends Perikatan activities, issues show-cause notice over Bersatu complaint
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Registrar of Societies (RoS) has issued a show-cause notice to the opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional (PN) and ordered an immediate suspension of all its activities nationwide. Following the notice, the regulator invoked Subsection 13(2A) of the Act to freeze all PN activities effective September 23. PN also confirmed receiving the separate suspension order, which halts all coalition operations until further notice.

items.title: 'There will be elections in Venezuela,' interim leader tells UN
items.summary: United Nations, United States, Sept 24, 2026 (AFP) - Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez thanked US President Donald Trump for restoring diplomatic ties and told the United Nations on Wednesday that "there will be elections" in the Latin American country. Rodriguez replaced president Nicolas Maduro following his ouster by US forces in January, and she has served as a pliant ally to Washington since then. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, she thanked the Trump administration "for their willingness to resume the path of diplomatic relations and cooperation with Venezuela."

items.title: Archaeological 'breakthrough' could confirm origins of Paris
items.summary: PARIS: An ancient wall discovered in central Paris was hailed as a "major breakthrough" on Wednesday, as the archaeological find may have settled a long-standing debate about the location of the city's original settlement. A roughly 20-metre (66-foot) wall dating from the Gallo-Roman period was discovered in Paris this summer beneath a hospital on the Ile de la Cite, a stone's throw from Notre Dame Cathedral, the French culture ministry said. The stone-and-wood find is thought to be a fragment of the ramparts of Lutetia – the ancient name for Paris – built by the Gallic Parisii tribe, which lived along the River Seine in the Iron Age.

items.title: As five pct Treasury yields lose shock value, investors start worrying about six pct
items.summary: LONDON: For years, five per cent on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield was viewed as the point at which global financial markets would start hitting turbulence. This month's breach of five per cent - something that has happened only briefly in recent decades - has forced investors to contemplate an unsettling question: What if six per cent is the new number that should be keeping them awake at night? MSCI's main world stocks index halved in value the last time the 10-year Treasury yield broke five per cent, which was just before the global financial crash.

items.title: US business activity hits five-year high but strong demand fuels inflation fears
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in September, fuelled by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. S&P Global said on Wednesday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month. The rise in the PMI reflected strong gains in both the services and manufacturing sectors.

items.title: Crew member killed, 27 evacuated after ship targeted near Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: ISTANBUL: One crew member was killed and 27 others were evacuated after a commercial vessel was targeted near Oman's Musandam Governorate overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, Omani authorities said Wednesday, Anadolu Ajansi reported. The Omani Maritime Security Centre said in a statement on the US social media platform X that a Royal Navy of Oman vessel, in coordination with relevant authorities, evacuated the crew of the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged commercial ship Cape Dao. "Twenty-seven crew members were evacuated and provided with the necessary medical care after the vessel was targeted 2.5 nautical miles off Musandam Governorate," the centre said.

items.title: US, China agree to extend trade truce by two months, work on bigger deal, Bessent says
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States and China have agreed to extend by two months a trade truce that was due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday. Wednesday's meeting lasted about 90 minutes, Treasury said. US officials last week said the delivery of rare earths by China was also lagging.

items.title: [UPDATED] PN activities suspended, not deregistered - RoS
items.summary: RoS said the suspension was made under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), following the notice issued to PN on Sept 22. "RoS issued a notice under subsection 13(2) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832) dated Sept 22, 2026, and a reasonable period was given to PN to respond to the notice. RoS said following the notice, it also issued a suspension order on all PN activities effective Sept 23.

items.title: Pantai hospitals equip Batu Pahat community with burn response skills
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Pantai Hospital Melaka and Pantai Hospital Batu Pahat have equipped residents with practical knowledge on managing burn injuries and responding to fire-related emergencies. The hospitals brought together healthcare professionals, emergency responders and members of the community for the Burn Awareness Campaign 2026 at Batu Pahat Mall recently. Pantai Hospital Melaka chief executive officer Dr Kevin Khoo said many burn injuries occur during everyday situations, making it important for people to know how to respond quickly and correctly.

items.title: USM takes research beyond the lab
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has secured RM1.202 million in new industry funding from Intel Malaysia and Micron Memory Malaysia. This gives fresh momentum to Malaysia's drive to build advanced semiconductor capability, develop highly specialised talent and move university research into industrial application. Intel Malaysia and Micron Memory Malaysia presented RM482,000 and RM720,000,respectively, to Rahman.

items.title: The dependent independent director
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Independent directors are expected to provide objective, impartial and independent judgement to the board. Their role is particularly important because they are supposed to challenge management, scrutinise major decisions, protect shareholders' interests and ensure that the board does not simply become a rubber stamp for executive management or dominant shareholders. An individual may satisfy the formal definition of an "independent director" while gradually becoming psychologically, financially or socially dependent on the company, its management or controlling shareholders.

items.title: World's largest sovereign wealth fund holds stake in Northern Solar [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia data shows Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM) holds 10 million Northern Solar shares, or 2.53 per cent. Separately, Norway's Statens pensjonsfond utland is listed with 9.97 million shares, or 2.52 per cent. On a simple aggregation, the two entries amount to 19.97 million shares, equivalent to about 5.05 per cent of Northern Solar.

items.title: US, China agree to extend trade truce by two months, work on bigger deal
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States and China have agreed to extend by two months a trade truce that was due to expire on Nov 10, allowing more time to work on a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday. Bessent made the remarks on Fox News hours after his second meeting in four days with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to prepare for a summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. Wednesday's meeting lasted about 90 minutes, Treasury said.

items.title: Airstrike hits Afghanistan's Kandahar city
items.summary: AFGHANISTAN: An airstrike hit the southern Afghan city of Kandahar on Thursday, home to the Taliban government's supreme leader, a resident told AFP. At least three civilians were killed in the strikes on eastern Afghanistan, the United Nations reported, which Pakistan said killed 28 militants. Security issues have proved a sticking point, especially Pakistan's demand that Afghanistan curb the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) militant group.

items.title: North Korean IT contractor found working remotely in New Zealand
items.summary: WELLINGTON: A North Korean IT worker used a fake identity to obtain remote work with a New Zealand company and then threatened to release sensitive information when exposed, Wellington's cybersecurity agency said Thursday. New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre said the IT contractor was working remotely for a large New Zealand business, which grew "suspicious" of his true identity over time. "Investigation identified the worker as being from North Korea," the report said.

items.title: Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Iowa newspaper and pollster
items.summary: WASHINGTON: An Iowa judge, citing First Amendment protections, dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit filed in late 2024 against the Des Moines Register newspaper and pollster J. Ann Selzer over a poll that showed the Republican leader trailing before the 2024 elections. "At its core, the Plaintiffs' Petition seeks to stretch both Iowa statutory and common law beyond their current bounds, turning speech that enjoys the highest category of First Amendment protection into a liability," Iowa District Judge Scott Beattie said in the ruling on Wednesday. Free speech group FIRE, which represented Selzer, welcomed the ruling.

items.title: Colombia president orders troops to violence-hit Caribbean city
items.summary: SANTA MARTA, (Colombia): Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella sent troops into the Caribbean city of Santa Marta on Tuesday after gunmen attacked shops and burnt vehicles following the killing of one of their leaders. De la Espriella said in a later video statement that he had ordered "that Santa Marta be militarised." De la Espriella said on X that he had arrived in Santa Marta to oversee the crackdown.

items.title: Son of Israel's US envoy injured in West Bank ramming attack
items.summary: RAMALLAH: Israeli ambassador to the US Yechiel Leiter said his son was the soldier injured in a car-ramming attack on Wednesday in the occupied West Bank. Israeli police said earlier a Palestinian man drove a car at high speed towards a policewoman and a soldier who were conducting vehicle searches at an intersection near the Israeli settlement of Beit Horon west of Ramallah. Ambassador Leiter said his son was the injured soldier, adding: "Neria needs a miracle."

items.title: UK air force fighter jet crashes on training exercise
items.summary: LONDON: UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting on Wednesday said an investigation was underway after an air force Hawk fighter jet crashed during a training exercise in north Wales. The Hawk T2 aircraft had been flying out of the Royal Air Force (RAF) Valley station on Anglesey, an island off the northwest coast of Wales. The Hawk T1 and newer T2 versions are transonic, two-seat training aircraft used to train fast jet pilots.

items.title: PH Plus seen as possible lifeline for Bersatu in Melaka [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An electoral understanding under the Pakatan Harapan Plus framework may be the most practical path forward for Bersatu following its split with Pas. Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Bersatu was likely to explore new electoral arrangements as going solo would be a high-risk option. On Saturday, Melaka PH said it was finalising negotiations with parties that shared similar aspirations, including Bersatu, to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka election.

items.title: What prolonged extreme heat means for Malaysia’s poultry: Growth slows, eggs dip, but no automatic shortage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — With Malaysia bracing for an intensification of El Niño conditions, prolonged extreme heat could affect the country’s poultry production, particularly if high temperatures persist for days or weeks. The effects could include slower growth in broiler chickens, higher mortality and lower egg production, potentially putting pressure on Malaysia’s chicken and egg supply. How could heat affect chicken production?

items.title: Judge urged to lift Trump's White House ban on media outlets
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A lawyer for CNN, MS NOW and Politico urged a US federal judge on Wednesday to immediately restore White House access for the news organisations after President Donald Trump abruptly revoked their credentials. CNN, MS NOW and Politico went to court after Trump on Friday ordered that they be barred from the White House as punishment for distributing what he called "fake news" and "fiction and lies." "Access to the White House is a privilege – not a right," it said.

items.title: FAA says Trump arch with signal flame got no special treatment in review
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The head of the US Federal Aviation Administration said on Wednesday there was no political interference in the agency's air safety review of President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch that will include an eternal flame for visibility. The proposed 250-foot (76-metre) arch would be 3,000 feet from Reagan Washington National Airport and within the airport's main approach and departure corridors. On Tuesday, US Representative Don Beyer said Trump's plan to base military drones at the arch would require the FAA to conduct a new safety analysis.

items.title: Turkiye to hand over military base to Iraq
items.summary: ANKARA: Turkiye will hand over control of its base in Bashiqa in northern Iraq to Baghdad, the Turkish presidency announced Wednesday in a joint statement with its neighbour. "In light of progress achieved by these security measures implemented by Iraq, Turkish forces will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zilkan base to the Federal Government of Iraq in accordance with the agreed mechanism and timetable," a joint statement said. Ankara returning Zilkan to Baghdad by agreed mechanism and timeline is one such thread: Iraqi sovereignty and Turkish security, both served," he posted on X.

items.title: Tesla's supervised self-driving system often misreads speed limits, Belgian safety group finds
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: Tesla's FSD automated-driving system frequently exceeded speed limits and attempted to overtake cyclists on streets where it is prohibited, a road-safety advocacy group said, citing tests it conducted in Belgium. It found that FSD often exceeded speed limits in 20km/h and 30km/h zones, and incorrectly displayed higher speed limits to drivers, potentially misleading them about how fast the vehicle should travel. Tesla's FSD driver-assistance feature can perform most driving tasks but requires drivers to pay strict attention.

items.title: Trump plans grand spectacle for potentially tense talks as Xi arrives in US
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit where the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Teheran will play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony. For the Chinese leader's first trip to the US in nearly three years, Trump was set to greet Xi and his wife on the tarmac, breaking with normal protocol. Xi's plane landed Wednesday evening at the Maryland military base that hosts Air Force One, where Trump was waiting.

items.title: UUCA replacement Bill expected to be tabled in December, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The first reading of the Bill to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) is expected to be tabled at the Dewan Rakyat sitting in December, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the ministry is working to complete a comprehensive series of engagements with stakeholders to ensure the Bill accounts for the entire national higher education ecosystem before it is tabled in Parliament. Meanwhile, turning to Budget 2027, Zambry expressed hope that the Higher Education Ministry would secure a larger allocation to support the Malaysian Higher Education Development Plan.

items.title: ADB raises Malaysia’s 2026, 2027 growth forecasts to 4.9pc, 4.7pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has raised its 2026 and 2027 economic growth forecasts for Malaysia to 4.9 per cent and 4.7 per cent, respectively. In its September 2026 report, ADB said Malaysia’s growth is expected to moderate slightly in the second half of 2026 (2H 2026) and in 2027. Domestic spending will likely remain resilient, but heightened downside pressures may limit labour and consumption growth, it said.

items.title: SPR: Postal voting applications for Melaka polls open today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 —Applications for all categories of domestic and overseas postal voting for the 16th Melaka State Election open today. Khairul Shahril said applications under Category 1A cover police and military personnel, election officials, EC members and staff, as well as media personnel. Melaka State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum also submitted the dissolution notice to the EC yesterday.

items.title: ‘Decision has been made’: Anthony Loke firm on resignation, to hand in letter upon return from China
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he remains firm in his decision to resign as Transport Minister. The Seremban MP said he would hand in his resignation letter upon returning home from China. I will submit the resignation letter to the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) when I return home,” he told reporters briefly after arriving in Hangzhou today.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidates to be announced one to two weeks ahead of nomination, says PM’s pol-sec
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 23 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said Prime Minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin. He said the move would allow PH to make early preparations instead of waiting until the last minute to finalise its candidates. Azman said the Ziarah Kasih programme was among the activities carried out by the Political Secretary’s Office and would continue in several other areas in Melaka, including the Jasin parliamentary constituency next week.

items.title: Police announce three‑stage road closures for Kuching Marathon from Sept 26 to 27
items.summary: These include the Jalan Pearl-Jalan Wawasan traffic lights towards Padang Merdeka, Lebuh Wayang-Jalan Wawasan, Jalan McDougall-Jalan Tun Abang Haji Openg, and Susur Jalan Haji Taha. Also affected are the Jalan Ajibah Abol traffic lights, Jalan Muhibbah-Jalan Kulas junction, Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob-Jalan Merdeka junction, Jalan Kampung Lintang-Jalan Astana traffic lights, Mahkamah roundabout, Sesco roundabout, and Samariang roundabout. The closures will also cover the Jalan Sultan Tengah traffic lights near the fire station and Sego, Yayasan roundabout, Kesuma Resort roundabout, Stadium roundabout, Gersik roundabout, Merrican Salleh-Jalan Kwong Lee Bank traffic lights, Tanah Putih Clinic traffic lights, Jalan Sekama-Pending traffic lights, Sri Aman roundabout, and Jalan Gamelan-Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob junction.

items.title: Man dies in suspected electrocution in Lahad Datu
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Sept 23 — A man in his 30s died after he was believed to have been electrocuted at Kampung Puyut here today. The man, who had yet to be identified, was believed to have no identification document and was not recognised by local villagers, said Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid. He said the department received a distress call at 12.47pm and deployed 12 personnel to the scene, where the man was found electrocuted and was later confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel.

items.title: Bring umbrellas: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in KL and 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states affected are Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kedah, the areas expected to be affected are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak. The same warning has been issued for Kelantan, covering Jeli and Kuala Krai; Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu); and Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut, Lipis and Kuantan).

items.title: Anwar: Negeri Sembilan MB and executive council’s bid to remove ruler was ‘rude and uncivilised’
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim criticised the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar and state executive council for attempting to remove Yang di‑Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, calling the move rude and uncivilised. He said no state‑level authority has the mandate to question or alter the position of the Ruler, according to Berita Harian . Anwar said the crisis involving state administration and customary authority in Negeri Sembilan had become increasingly complex.

items.title: Anwar asks Loke to review decision to quit Cabinet after Najib’s conditional pardon
items.summary: HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Transport Minister Anthony Loke to rethink his plan to step down from the Cabinet following the Pardons Board’s decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon. In a New Straits Times report, Anwar said DAP should not give in to political pressure from groups seeking instability in the unity government. “Some people ask, why Anthony Loke?

items.title: Structural checks at Cheras apartment will take several days following landslide, says Selangor exco
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Residents evacuated from Block D of the Damai Perdana Apartments in Cheras may have to remain out of their homes for several days while authorities determine whether the building is structurally safe. Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Zone 6 councillor Tan Kah Hoe said multiple technical agencies were conducting assessments of the affected block, according to New Straits Times . Residents of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras were ordered to evacuate their homes last night after a landslide occurred near the building, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak.

items.title: Sabah man bites ex-girlfriend and threatens to kill her, gets RM5,800 fine
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — A 35-year-old man was fined RM5,800 after pleading guilty to hurting his ex-girlfriend and threatening to kill her. Mohd Aideed Husein pleaded guilty before two Magistrates, Dzul Elmy Yunus and Marilyn Kelvin, to separate charges over the incident involving the 30-year-old woman on Sept 15. Before Dzul Elmy, he was fined RM1,800, in default six months’ jail, under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to the woman outside a shop at Lorong Suria Inanam 1.

items.title: Expedite court proceedings to settle Negeri Sembilan royal dispute, says ex-minister Syed Hamid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Court proceedings related to the Negeri Sembilan royal institution dispute should be expedited to provide a definitive resolution to the legal questions involved, former law minister Tan Sri Syed Hamid Albar said. He said the dispute, which involves the adat (customary practices), state law and the Federal Constitution, should be resolved through the legal process rather than public debate or sentiment. Syed Hamid also urged all parties to refrain from making conflicting public statements, saying these could heighten public anxiety and make it more difficult to reach a reasonable and rational resolution.

items.title: TVET graduates may have jobs, but are they the right jobs? MEF asks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called for a broader assessment of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduate employability to better reflect their skills, career progression and contribution to the workforce. MEF senior adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the federation supported Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir’s call for the employability of Polytechnic and Community College (PolyCC) graduates to be assessed beyond headline employment percentages. He said the 2025 employability rates of 98.5 per cent for polytechnic graduates and 98.8 per cent for community college graduates were encouraging, but the quality and relevance of employment should also be considered in evaluating TVET outcomes.

items.title: Kota Bharu trader’s no-show lands him an arrest warrant over 42 cooking oil charges
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — The Sessions Court here today issued an arrest warrant for the owner of a subsidised cooking oil business after he failed to appear before the court to face charges involving the management of records and documents for the controlled item. Judge Nik Habri Muhamad issued the arrest warrant for Pui Tiong Lam, 61, for failing to appear in court for today’s prosecution proceedings without a valid reason. The court set Nov 5 for mention.

items.title: AG says Negeri Sembilan state secretary and legal adviser remain in office, must continue duties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Negeri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal must continue carrying out their duties because their suspension by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is invalid. Dusuki said, “The duties of Mohd Zafir as Negeri Sembilan state secretary and Muzalmah as state legal adviser must continue as usual, and they must also remain in Negeri Sembilan.” Dusuki said the situation in Negeri Sembilan mirrors the 2009 Perak crisis, when the state secretary and state legal adviser were also suspended.

items.title: Kelantan telecoms at risk of major outages as cable vandalism and theft soar, says says regional MCMC official
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — Vandalism and theft of telecommunications infrastructure in Kelantan have reached an alarming level and could disrupt communication coverage and the livelihoods of people if critical infrastructure is affected. Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Eastern Region Office senior director Mohd Fairus Muhamad said these incidents have also impacted the telecommunications industry, which bears millions of ringgit in losses for repair and restoration work. He said MCMC, together with enforcement authorities and industry players, is tightening coordination, including proposing a Telecommunications Infrastructure Vandalism Prevention Sub-Committee involving MCMC, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), local authorities, the Land and District Office and industry players.

items.title: Psychosis impaired teen’s understanding he was taking a life in Bandar Utama school murder, court says, rejecting months‑long planning claim
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — The Shah Alam High Court rejected claims that the 16-year-old schoolgirl’s murder in Bandar Utama last year was planned for months, finding that the accused’s psychotic illness impaired his understanding of the act and that the alleged “plan” stemmed from his delusions. In her full written grounds, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said she could not accept that merely knowing he was pushing a knife into the deceased’s abdomen and that it would cause her to bleed was sufficient to establish that the accused understood the nature of the act. She added that an accused who has knowledge of the mechanics but not of the reality of what he is doing cannot be said to know the nature of the act.

items.title: Budget 2027 wishlist: Rehda wants wider housing loan access, special campaign for unsold units
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Enhancing the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) and introducing improved financing structures are among the proposals made by the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) Malaysia for Budget 2027. The association is also seeking an extension of existing stamp duty relief and a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) for unsold completed residential units. Rehda also proposed government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms, as well as stepped-up financing structures that would allow lower repayments during the initial years of house ownership.

items.title: Who was he? A month on, mystery deepens over man found dead in KLIA aircraft landing gear
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 23 — The identity of a man whose body was found in an aircraft’s landing gear compartment at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2 on Aug 27 remains unknown and the remains have yet to be claimed. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said police had yet to receive any information that could establish the man’s identity. Asked how the man came to be inside the aircraft, Shazeli said the circumstances remained a mystery and were still under investigation.

items.title: Former Kelantan Kafa teacher gets RM2,000 fine for kicking Year Five pupil in face during class
items.summary: KUALA KRAI, Sept 23 — A former Religious and Fardu Ain Class (Kafa) teacher was fined RM2,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today for kicking a Year Five pupil in the face, causing injuries to his gums. Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid imposed the maximum fine, with a default of four months in jail, after Abdullah Mustakim, 33, pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to the pupil in a classroom at a school here at about 2.30 pm on Oct 23, 2024. The kick caused an injury to the pupil’s gums.

items.title: Anwar courts Chinese industry leaders with eye on investments in chips, AI and robotics
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — A roundtable discussion with industry leaders from 21 leading Chinese companies here focused on various high-impact sectors, including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics, as Malaysia explores high-value strategic investments, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The discussion also touched on the potential of electric vehicles (EVs), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology, healthcare, specialty chemicals and advanced manufacturing. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook also participated in the discussion.

items.title: Rosmah’s RM67.5m jewellery bill: No pause button, Court of Appeal rules
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 23 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has lost her latest bid to fully halt a RM67.5 million payment owed to Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL over dozens of missing jewellery pieces. The Court of Appeal has dismissed her appeal against a High Court order for a conditional stay, meaning the sum must still be deposited into a stakeholder account within a month of the August 12 judgement, The Edge reported today. The dispute traces back to a June High Court ruling by Judicial Commissioner Datuk Quay Chew Soon, which held Rosmah liable for 43 pieces of jewellery that went missing after a 2018 police raid.

items.title: Zero motions, zero Bills: Dewan Rakyat Speaker still waiting on no-confidence bid, PM term-limit, and AG-PP split
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 23 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said he has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting. Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure. Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.

items.title: Three-day remand for two men as Sarawak police probe convenience store fire cases
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Two men aged 40 and 23 were remanded for three days by the Magistrates’ Court here today to assist investigations into a case of mischief by fire involving a convenience store along Jalan Green here. The court ordered both suspects to be remanded for three days from Sept 23 to Sept 26 to assist investigations under Section 436 of the Penal Code. Three suspects have been arrested and remanded to assist investigations into both incidents.

items.title: Haze eases in Lubok Antu, but Kanowit air remains ‘very unhealthy’ at midday
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Lubok Antu moved out of the very unhealthy category by noon today after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading dropped from 205 at 8am to 195. Most monitoring stations across Sarawak also remained in the unhealthy category at noon, with readings ranging from 105 to 195. Under the API classification, readings of 0–50 are considered good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy and 201–300 very unhealthy.
